correctness.rationale: Indicator expansion with at most five excluded parameters each costing at most four gives \(8N\ge\sum I-20\). The exact single sums are \((-1,0,-1)\); the squarefree cubic character sums have absolute value at most \(2\sqrt p\) each; the squarefree quartic has \(|S+1|\le2\sqrt p\) because its smooth genus-one completion has two rational points at infinity; the squarefree quintic has \(|S|\le4\sqrt p\) by genus-two Hasse–Weil. Hence \(8N\ge p-23-10\sqrt p>0\) for every \(p\ge149\). All \(33\) odd primes below \(149\) were exhaustively enumerated twice by independent exact character algorithms; their complete failing set is \(\{3,5,7,13,17,29\}\); at \(29\) precisely two mixed words are absent.

value.rationale: The six mixed residue/nonresidue configurations of the classical normalized Pythagorean parametrization are a natural complement to published monochromatic and full-two-parameter questions. This theorem gives an exact necessary-and-sufficient prime classification, a sharp universal threshold p=31, and all exceptional sign-pattern obstructions.
